# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 24–33/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 33. All results are read from code. `robots.txt` tells every crawler to stay out of the whole site, and the pages are built in the browser, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript see an empty page. The one unknown is the canonical link (the tag that names a page's main address). I can't judge it without knowing your domain. The 40-point cap for a quotable blocker did not apply, because the one blocker I found, `robots.txt` answering with a server error, is not present. ## Live check **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks every crawler, including search and AI search crawlers, not to read any page. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50–59. GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become Clear. This assumes you want to be found, which I assumed because there is no `geo.config.json`. If the block is deliberate, tell me and I will change that assumption. ### 2. Render page content on the server or prerender it - **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends, and here that is an empty page. - **Where:** `index.html:8` and `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
`, and the catalogue loads its items only in the browser with `fetch('/api/mugs')` inside `useEffect`. - **Size:** Large - **Score after this:** adds 3 points, about 13 points on the score, on top of item 1. ### 3. Add a sitemap, then real titles, descriptions and `lang` - **Why it matters:** a sitemap is the list of pages you want found, and the title and description are what crawlers read first about each page. The sitemap is worth 2 points and the head tags another 2. - **Where:** there is no sitemap file. The head is at `index.html:2` and `index.html:5`. - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App`, with no meta description. - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** adds about 17 points, 4 of 23, on top of item 1. The new `robots.txt` also needs an absolute `Sitemap:` line. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and small | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, 2 lines of valid syntax | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can access the site | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2`, `Disallow: /` under `User-agent: *` | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/catalogue` are both blocked by `public/robots.txt:2`. There is no noindex tag. | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical tag in `index.html`, and no domain is declared | | GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `index.html:8`. Both routes are client-only, and the catalogue data is fetched in `useEffect`. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Problem | Not run | No sitemap, and no `Sitemap:` line in `public/robots.txt` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | Not run | `index.html:5` has `Vite App`, there is no description, and `` has no `lang`. Both routes share this. | | GEO-016 | Routes reachable by normal links | Problem | Not run | `src/main.jsx:11` reaches `/catalogue` only through a button. 0 of 1 non-home routes are clear. | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` in the 5 source files, and no header code | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5` has an `` with no `alt`. `/` is a Problem and `/catalogue` is Clear, so it earns 0.5 of 1. I read the shared Nav and both pages. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | No `public/llms.txt`. Not scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Not scored. | Also in GEO-016: change the nav button at `src/main.jsx:11` to ``. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** there is no canonical tag and no declared domain. Tell me your site's domain, or add `site.origin` to `geo.config.json`, and I can judge it. If a canonical is missing on every page, the rule becomes a Problem. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. After you fix `robots.txt`, run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Hosting headers:** an `X-Robots-Tag` header set outside this repository would not show up here. This affects GEO-014 and GEO-017. - **Catalogue data:** `/api/mugs` is loaded at runtime, so I can't see what content it returns. ## Assumptions - You want search and AI search tools to find this site. There is no `geo.config.json`. - The two routes in `src/main.jsx` (`/` and `/catalogue`) are all the routes there are, so I sampled both. - Blocking training crawlers such as `GPTBot` is a separate choice. It doesn't affect the score. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
